chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 92 — The Righteous Will Awaken
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest primary-language witnesses responsibly available for this chapter. The surviving Aramaic of 4QEnochᵍ (4Q212), columns ii–iii, governs its extant wording in 92:1–2 and 92:5, including the fuller address to Methuselah, his brothers, descendants, and future generations. A small Greek remnant in the Chester Beatty–Michigan papyrus independently preserves parts of the opening scribal title and the closing condemnation of wickedness. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann’s 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, printed page 76, supplies all five verses and all wording not extant in the earlier fragments. The long Aramaic lacuna between verses 2 and 5 is not supplied beyond the complete transmitted Geʽez text. No modern English translation was used as the translation base, no commentary was used as Scripture, and no text absent from the primary witnesses was supplied.

verses.text: This is what Enoch wrote and gave to Methuselah his son and to all his brothers—Enoch, the distinguished scribe, wisest of men, and chosen from the sons of earth to judge their deeds. He also wrote it for his descendants and future generations, for all who dwell on the dry land and will practice goodness and peace.
verses.study: The fuller Aramaic opening presents the epistle as both family instruction and a message for the whole inhabited earth. Enoch's scribal calling binds clear testimony to the practice of goodness and peace.
crossReferences: 1 Enoch 91:1–3 — Enoch first gives the instruction to Methuselah and his family
Jude 14–15 — Enoch's witness is directed toward later generations and their deeds

verses.text: Do not be distressed, and do not let your spirits be troubled because of the times, for the Great Holy One has appointed days for everything.
verses.study: Distressing times do not lie outside divine appointment. Enoch grounds courage in the Great Holy One's sovereignty over seasons rather than in favorable circumstances.
crossReferences: Ecclesiastes 3:1 — every matter has an appointed time
Daniel 2:21 — God changes times and seasons

verses.text: The righteous will awaken from sleep, rise, and walk in the path of righteousness. His entire path and conduct will be in everlasting goodness and grace.
verses.study: Awakening leads immediately to a way of life. The righteous future is described not only as restored existence but as enduring conduct shaped by goodness and grace.
crossReferences: Daniel 12:2–3 — sleepers awaken and the wise shine
Isaiah 35:8–10 — the redeemed walk on the holy way with everlasting joy

verses.text: He will show grace to the righteous and give him everlasting uprightness. He will give him authority, and he will live in goodness and righteousness and walk in everlasting light.
verses.study: The righteous receive uprightness, authority, and light as gifts. Grace does not compete with righteousness here; it establishes the lasting life in which righteousness can flourish.
crossReferences: Isaiah 60:19–21 — everlasting light accompanies a wholly righteous people
Daniel 7:18 — the holy ones receive the kingdom forever

verses.text: Sin will perish in darkness forever and will never be visible again from that day onward, throughout all generations forever.
verses.study: The chapter closes with sin removed from sight and history. Darkness becomes its destination, while the righteous walk in the everlasting light named in the preceding verse.
crossReferences: Psalm 37:10 — the wicked are sought but are no longer found
Revelation 21:27 — nothing defiled enters the everlasting holy city

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 92 formally widens Enoch’s instruction beyond his immediate family. The earlier Aramaic presents him as a distinguished scribe and addresses descendants, future generations, and all who live on the earth in order to practice goodness and peace.

The command not to be distressed does not deny the severity of the times described in Chapter 91. It places every season under the appointment of the Great Holy One, giving the faithful a reason to persevere without surrendering to fear.

The righteous awakening unites restored life with restored conduct. Rising from sleep leads to walking in righteousness, goodness, grace, authority, and light. The future hope therefore transforms both existence and character.

Sin receives the opposite destination. It disappears into darkness and does not return, while the righteous inhabit everlasting light. The contrast completes the two-path teaching: what people choose to walk now anticipates the enduring world to which each path leads.

crossReferences: 1 Enoch 91:1–19 — the family instruction and the two paths
Psalm 1:1–6 — righteous and wicked paths reach different ends
Isaiah 60:19–21 — everlasting light and a righteous people
Daniel 2:20–22 — God rules times and reveals what is hidden
Daniel 7:18, 27 — the holy ones receive everlasting authority
Daniel 12:2–3 — awakening and the radiance of the wise
John 5:28–29 — resurrection leads toward life or judgment
